alerts.title: TDF nephrotoxicity risk: hypertension, NSAID use, trace proteinuria
alerts.message: Guidelines advise TDF be avoided if eGFR < 50 mL/min/1.73m2 and recommend closer renal monitoring in high-risk patients, particularly those with co-existent hypertension. This patient has sub-optimally controlled hypertension (146/94), trace proteinuria on dipstick, and regular ibuprofen use, a combination that compounds nephrotoxicity risk. Creatinine is 112 umol/L today, but no eGFR is recorded and the guideline schedule requires eGFR at 3, 6 and then 6-12 monthly. Proteinuria is attributed to hypertension in the plan, but TDF-associated tubular injury is not excluded; the excerpts do not establish a causal link either way from today's data alone.

evidence.recommended_action: Calculate eGFR today and repeat per schedule; consider urine protein quantification; minimise or avoid NSAIDs; review TDF suitability with renal risk in mind, and urgently review if eGFR falls below 50.

alerts.title: Low serum phosphate with proteinuria suggests possible TDF tubulopathy
alerts.message: Serum phosphate is 0.78 mmol/L today, below normal, alongside trace proteinuria. TDF can cause renal tubular wasting syndrome, which presents with hypophosphataemia and proteinuria. Non-drug causes (hypertension-related damage, poor intake) are also possible. The excerpts identify tubular wasting as a TDF adverse effect but do not give a phosphate threshold, so this finding is not addressed in the plan.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat serum phosphate, measure urine protein and assess for Fanconi-type features; if TDF tubulopathy is suspected, discuss switching to an alternative NtRTI such as TAF per guideline options.
